html:
On 7 December 1975 Indonesian troops invaded East Timor, landing at Dili. In 1976 Suharto's government declared it Indonesia's 27th province.

Indonesia acted with the quiet consent of the United States and Australia, who feared a left-wing state during the Cold War. The United Nations never recognised the annexation.

Fighting, famine and forced moves followed, especially in the late 1970s. A truth commission later counted at least 100,000 deaths caused by the conflict, out of a population of about 650,000. Resistance led by Fretilin continued until the 1999 vote.
sum: On 7 December 1975 Indonesian troops invaded East Timor, landing at Dili. In 1976 Suharto's government declared it Indonesia's 27th province.
